candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — health teaching and injury prevention
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — occupational safety education
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize worker safety training as proactive education for hazard identification, reporting, controls, and safe work practices.

options.A: Teach workers to recognize and report hazards, understand the controls used for those hazards, and follow required safe work practices and protective measures.
options.B: Leave hazard recognition entirely to supervisors so frontline workers do not need information about workplace risks or controls.
options.C: Provide safety training only after an injury occurs because preventive training before an incident has little value.
options.D: Treat initial orientation as sufficient even when a worker receives a new task or is exposed to a new hazard.

candidate.rationale: OSHA identifies education and training as a core safety-program element. Workers need to understand hazards, how to report them, the controls used, and safe work practices; additional training is needed when tasks or hazards change. B through D undermine those prevention principles.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Effective safety training gives workers knowledge and skills to recognize/report hazards, understand controls, and work safely, including retraining for changed tasks/hazards.
candidate.source_document_title: Education and Training — Recommended Practices for Safety and Health Programs
candidate.source_locator: Education and Training overview; Action Item 4 — Train workers on hazard identification and controls
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
candidate.stem: A community health nurse is helping an employer plan worker safety education. What is a core purpose of effective safety training?
